en: No, I just happened to see you, so I
thought I'd say hello
Cleaning takes more muscle than you'd think.
Folks like you get worn out in no time.
What, back again?
You're an odd one.
Is there something you need from me?
<Do you follow current affairs?>
<Please show me how to clean>
Huh? I couldn't care less about that.
All I want to know is tomorrow's weather.
Ha ha ha, then you asked the right person.
Put your heart into it. That goes for anything.
Not that I'm old enough for that, really.
I'm sorry. I've only just moved here,
so I thought I'd come and say hello
I may not look it, but I'm busy, you know.
You get an awfully troubled look sometimes.
Sigh... You're a worry, lad.
Did you leave your family to come to London?
I know how lonely that can feel.
But it's the path you chose, so hang in there.
Ah, Master...
I'll gladly work for your sake, Master...
Ugh, everything just gets on my nerves.
My body aches, I'm worn out, the pay's low...
Whatever you wish, just say the word...
Lately I'm worn out even after sleeping.
Huh? What's with you?
Who are you? Don't get so familiar with me.
Pardon me, my lady.
A lady? Where d'you see a lady?
I'm just a lowly maid.
The name's Claudia.
By rights I'd want no part of this rotten job,
but I do the laundry at that noble's house.
It's hard, the pay's poor, it's no good at all.
(Hmph... a noisy woman.
But she looks sturdy. She'd do as a servant.)
Ah, busy, busy
grumble, grumble
note: follows #152 '...'; leading space so it reads 'busy, busy... grumble, grumble...'

en: Well, well, it's you! Mornin'.
Lucky you. You look like you've nothing to do.
Ugh, just thinking about work gets me down.
Hey, you!
It's me, see? Claudia the laundress.
Up close, you're quite a handsome man...
I had a sweetheart like you once, too.
I was a beauty no man could leave alone.
Good evening. Excuse me a moment.
What? I'm dead tired already.
If it's a stupid question, ask someone else.
I'm new to London and hoped to ask the way.
Would you tell me, my lady...?
Claudia.
Calling me 'lady'? Spare me the cheap flattery.
Want directions? See that big clock tower,
Big Ben? Walk straight on until you reach it,
and then ask someone else who's there.
It's no use asking me anything.
Oh, it's you. We've met before.
Sigh... Must be nice, being so carefree.
Just wandering about with nothing to do.
Hey, you,
, wasn't it?
Are you keeping well?
And how is your work going?
Oh, just listen to this
My master gets his shirts dirty in no time,
drops his clothes wherever he takes them off,
and puts his socks on inside out,
Honestly, I'm not his nursemaid, you know.
I work this hard and the pay's still poor,
and they make me do more than washing
Glad to see you're well. Good day to you.
note: player line (stern) though used_in labels it Claudia; she protests in msg 263148

en: Oh, h-hey, wait, I'm not finished
Some people! Listen when someone's talking to you
Ugh, how long will I be stuck in this job?
